evidence.upstream fix: the MESH branch now reads texcoord_offset = mesh_texcoord_offsets[mesh_id] and skips the lookup when it is negative, leaving uv at (0,0). The comment names mjm.mesh_texcoordadr == -1 -- exactly the condition Step-7 W5 diagnosed on OGBScene's two stopbuttonrim geoms (examples/results/step7/ogb-manipulation/findings.md S11)
evidence.why that is not a contradiction: stable_envs.render.mjwarp.texture_gaps describes the MODEL (a textured mesh with no UVs), not the renderer's tolerance of it. The model has not changed, so the report has not. What changed is that mujoco_warp no longer dies on it

2_existing_evidence_rechecked.answer: YES, and it does not hold

evidence.consequence: 0.533854 under 3.12 (the bound, to 4e-6) -> 0.522233 under 3.13, which is BELOW the floor. A 3.13 bump turns a passing family_specific Gate-A check into a FAIL on a cell the texcoord defect never touched

DMCCheetahRun.caveat: this cell's oracle digest is documented as NOT run-to-run reproducible (mujoco_warp's batched render; examples/results/step6/texture-fidelity/findings.md S5), so the digest alone is not the evidence here -- the fidelity and downsample numbers below are

FetchReach.why: gymnasium-robotics' set_joint_qpos assertion fires under mujoco >= 3.12, so the Fetch REFERENCE env cannot be built at all on 3.12 or 3.13. This is upstream and predates 3.13 (docs/research/swm_matrix.md); it is recorded here because a bump would make it the shipped configuration

evidence.reading: each of these is plausibly a correctness improvement upstream. None of them is the texcoord fix, and every one of them can move a pixel in a cell that has no textured mesh at all. That is what condition 3 asks about, and the digests confirm it in the frames
render.py changes beyond the texcoord gu: vertex_normal(): a vertex normal more than ~37 degrees off its face is replaced by the face normal (matching mjr_uploadMesh) -- a SHADING change on every mesh

BVH traversal widened by RAY_TOL_REL / RAY_TOL_ABS and coincident hits now tie-break to the higher geom index 'like MuJoCo's GL depth test' -- a VISIBILITY change on every scene with touching surfaces
the no-light fallback is now a shadow_light_fraction parameter rather than the NO_LIGHT_AMBIENT_FALLBACK constant -- a LIGHTING change
a new _aa_resolve kernel accumulates and averages samples -- a SAMPLING change

control.built_from: $SCR/venvs/se7-ogb's pin set with ONLY the MuJoCo pair bumped
control.hardware: SLURM allocation 6443480, gpu2264, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, driver 575.57.08, MUJOCO_GL=egl
other_differences: stable-worldmodel 0.1.1 added --no-deps for the OGB arm

recommendation_why: Condition 1 holds and conditions 2 and 3 do not. mujoco_warp 3.13.0 does fix the UV-less-mesh crash -- the guard is in the shipped source and names the exact field -- but the same release also changes ray tie-breaking, vertex normals, the no-light fallback and sample resolution, and every frozen digest measured here moves: OGBCube, OGBScene and DMCCheetahRun. DMCCheetahRun's downsample number crosses its frozen floor, so the bump would create a Gate-A FAIL. And the bump buys nothing that is currently costing anything: OGBScene already renders, because the cell bakes the unsamplable material away, at a DECLARED residual of 0.139 % of pixels with interior_exact 1.0. Dropping that bake under 3.13 would itself change pixels and need a re-declaration. Separately, mujoco >= 3.12 cannot build the Fetch reference env at all, so 3.13 is not a candidate for the interpreter that certifies Fetch either.
what_this_is: the mujoco / mujoco-warp 3.13.0 bump evaluation against plan section 14's three conditions, assembled from committed measurement arms. No pin is changed by this workstream; this is a recommendation.
what_would_change_the_answer: a release that carries the texcoord guard and NOTHING else in the render path, or a deliberate re-declaration campaign that re-measures every mjwarp cell under the new pair and re-freezes with the drift documented. Both are Step-9 scope. Until then the finding to record upstream is that the fix and the renderer changes shipped together.
